required_claims.text: Bridging 3+ scales simultaneously remains rare
required_claims.evidence: van2025: no FM architecture specifically designed for multiscale problems exists; MuMMI cited as the lone example connecting three resolutions (1000 nm / 30 nm CG / all-atom). nguyen2023: hierarchical schemes memory-bound, concurrent schemes compute-bound, both limiting scalability.
required_claims.caveat: Neither source states rarity as a counted fact; they state absence of dedicated architectures and the mechanism making coupling costly.
required_claims.flag: verify — negative existence claim, source literature cutoff ~mid-2025

required_claims.text: Labeled multiscale datasets are expensive and scarce
required_claims.evidence: nguyen2023: experimental data collection expensive and tedious, synthetic data computationally demanding, scarcity causes overfitting; named first pressing issue. van2025: multiscale datasets not yet well established; Table 3 shows datasets skewed to inorganic atomic-scale, gap at meso/macro and for polymers/composites.

required_claims.text: MLIP/model transferability across composition and phase space
required_claims.evidence: li2025_ood: leave-one-element/group/period-out over 700 tasks; 85% of leave-one-element-out tasks R²>0.95 (ALIGNN), failures on H, F, O. jakob2025: 100 target compositions, 41826 host structures, 161273 trial structures; convex-hull and polymorph ordering largely preserved.

required_claims.text: MLIP transferability across temperature and pressure
required_claims.evidence: van2025: materials behave differently at extreme temperature/pressure; current models focus on equilibrium properties, temperature-dependent ones less explored — stated, not measured. jakob2025: flags need for high-pressure-stable general purpose MLIPs as open direction.
required_claims.caveat: No source in this set benchmarks temperature as a generalization axis. Deng uses 1000 K MD only as a sampling device.

required_claims.text: Model interpretability ("black box")
required_claims.evidence: nguyen2023: black-box nature undermines trustworthiness; physics-naïve architectures achieve high accuracy yet fail to capture physical laws. van2025: interpretability degrades with model scale; generative models produce syntactically valid but physically implausible outputs.
required_claims.distractor_note: li2025_ood Fig. 1b / Methods uses SHAP and UMAP+KDE as diagnostics, not as an unsolved barrier. An answer claiming these solve interpretability is wrong.

required_claims.evidence: deng2025_softening: 147 surfaces / 29 systems, 470 Mg migration paths / 110 structures; softening scale <1 for >90% of 1000 WBM compounds. jakob2025: false-positive rates below hull 56% (M3GNet) / 30% (MACE-MP-0) vs 7% for DFT; ΔE_GS RMSE 175 / 117 meV/atom. li2025_ood: 92% of the '≥5 elements' test set inside the representational training domain.

required_claims.text: OOD error is systematic bias, not noise, and traces to training sets biased toward near-equilibrium low-energy configurations

required_claims.evidence: deng2025_softening: PES softening from underpredicted curvature, relaxation trajectories near local minima. jakob2025: over-stabilization of metastable minima growing with ΔE_GS. li2025_ood: H/F/O formation energies overpredicted by all models, removable by linear correction.

Center, nu=3 fixed with L=0/1/2: -0.64 / -0.63 / -0.64, i.e. equivariance shifts the curve without changing the exponent. MACE L=0 often nearly matches or exceeds competitive equivariant models (3BPA 1200 K: L=0 E 37.1 / F 81.6 vs NequIP L=3 38.5 / 76.2). The paper locates the defect in two-body messages being non-universal approximators, citing Pozdnyakov and Ceriotti, not in invariance as such, and states two independent routes to fix it.

required_claims.text: Data efficiency here means sample efficiency only; equivariance carries a compute cost that the founding evidence does not quantify

locations.batatia2022: Sec. 5.2, Computational Cost; Table 2, Time latency row

required_claims.evidence: batatia2022: names the equivariant tensor product as the computational bottleneck of equivariant MPNNs; single-codebase latencies MACE L=0 10.5 ms, L=1 17.5, L=2 24.3 vs NequIP 103.5 and BOTNet 101.2. park2024: message passing extends the receptive field well beyond rc, so communication in spatial decomposition scales with rc times the number of layers; strong-scaling speed-up 13.1-15.4 on 32 GPUs against an ideal 32.
required_claims.caveat: No source in this set gives a controlled compute comparison of equivariant vs invariant at matched accuracy. batzner2022 reports no inference-time or throughput figures at all, so the sample-efficiency result cannot be read as an efficiency result.
required_claims.flag: verify — as of 2026 fused tensor-product kernels (FlashTP, cuEquivariance, OpenEquivariance) have materially changed this cost picture; any cost statement must be dated

required_claims.text: The claim that deep message passing prevents parallelization is architectural, not fundamental: an adapted spatial-decomposition algorithm retains high weak-scaling efficiency at five layers
required_claims.evidence: batatia2022 asserts that decoupling correlation order from iteration count keeps the receptive field small and the model parallelisable. park2024 restricts inter-processor communication to the original rc by exchanging node features and gradients per layer: five-layer models hold 0.95-1.0 weak-scaling efficiency at 2 GPUs and 0.79-0.84 at 32, against 0.83-0.98 and 0.67-0.83 for two-layer models; efficiency rises slightly with more channels and layers because compute grows faster than communication. required_claims.text: The advantage is regime-dependent: at 10^6-10^7 training structures unconstrained architectures match equivariant ones on accuracy, with the residual cost appearing as training epochs rather than as an accuracy ceiling

Bin 5 geometry success 66.7/75.0/66.7/66.7/58.3%; Em success 16.7/0/16.7/8.3/0%. Only two models achieve >0.5 on both metrics, and only in bin 1. required_claims.text: One response to the transferability limit is architectural avoidance: designing the method so that the model is queried only on configurations close to its training distribution, rather than improving generalization

locations.maevskiy2025: Abstract; Sec. I final paragraphs; Sec. II.A opening; Appendix C

required_claims.evidence: Stated design principle: generalization error of the ML-IAP is assumed reduced when the system under study differs from the closest training object by only the coordinates of a single atom, rather than by all atomic positions. Hence the frozen-framework approximation — one mobile ion on a grid, remaining atoms fixed — with grid step <=0.25 A and exclusion of sites within R_min = 1.2 A of other atoms to avoid unphysical configurations. Abstract frames the method as requiring minimal generalization capabilities. Authors contrast this explicitly with active learning, which reduces generalization error but sacrifices the efficiency gained by replacing DFT. Two consequences: (i) hand-crafted Xi outperforms trained multivariate models — logistic regression with L1/L2 and CatBoost on PES descriptors, matminer descriptors, and both combined, none outperform Xi; (ii) the method generalizes to a chemical family absent from tuning data — hydroborates dominate the top of the Xi-ranked list although neither Kahle2020 nor Laskowski2023 contains positively labelled hydroborate electrolytes. Cost: 5997 structures in 7 days on one machine, versus the same time for ML-driven MD on 100 materials; ~50x faster than MLIP-MD, >=3000x than AIMD.
required_claims.caveat: Authors acknowledge the descriptors cannot capture the full complexity of the dynamical effects defining ionic conductivity; the 39% low-conductivity fraction in C1 is the visible cost of the static approximation.
required_claims.flag: novel claim type — about how the field responds to the transferability limit, not about the limit itself. Places maevskiy2025 and nam2025 as opposite strategies: avoid the OOD regime vs. train a surrogate that enters it.

required_claims.text: Permutation invariance is obtained in two places: order-independent aggregation over a neighbourhood, and a readout acting on the set of node states

locations.gilmer2017: Sec. 2, Eq. 1 and prose following Eq. 3; Sec. 1 para. 3; Sec. 3 para. 5; Sec. 5.4

required_claims.evidence: gilmer2017: the message to node v is a sum over neighbours N(v) (Eq. 1); the readout R operates on the set of node states and must be invariant to permutations of those states in order for the MPNN to be invariant to graph isomorphism; Sec. 5.4 shows the tower-mixing step preserves node-permutation invariance; Sec. 3 contrasts Behler-Parrinello representations, described as manifestly isomorphism-invariant, with the Coulomb matrix, where the invariance must instead be learned through dataset augmentation. jacobs2025 names permutations, translation and rotation as the symmetries an atomic environment featurization must respect.
required_claims.caveat: An answer attributing permutation invariance to message-passing aggregation ALONE is incomplete: aggregation carries local ordering, the readout carries global node ordering.
required_claims.distractor_note: geiger2022 Sec. 7.4 (ReducedTensorProduct, index formulas such as 'ijkl = jikl = klij') concerns permutation of tensor indices within one geometric object, NOT permutation of atoms. High lexical overlap, null semantic match. Citing geiger2022 Sec. 7.4 here is wrong.

required_claims.text: Translation invariance is obtained by operating on relative interatomic position vectors rather than absolute coordinates

locations.geiger2022: Sec. 8, Eq. 27 line 2; Sec. 8 code listing line 41

required_claims.evidence: geiger2022 Eq. 27 states P({x + a}) = P({x}) explicitly, and the accompanying module evaluates spherical harmonics on pos[e_src] - pos[e_dst], i.e. on relative position vectors. jacobs2025 writes the local atomic environment as densities over neighbour positions relative to a target atom.
required_claims.caveat: gilmer2017 Sec. 6 uses pairwise Euclidean distances, which does confer translation invariance, but the paper never states this as a rationale - the binning is justified by inspecting a histogram and the bins are hand-chosen. Cite gilmer2017 for mechanism only, never for justification.

required_claims.text: One rotational treatment builds scalar invariants from radial and angular basis functions and feeds only scalars to the model
required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025: the local atomic environment is written as a set of densities and expanded in a basis of radial and angular functions (Bessel and spherical harmonics respectively); tensor products over the target atom and its neighbours give values covariant with symmetry operations, and it is common to retain only the scalar-covariant (invariant) features, which can then be used in almost any continuously differentiable ML model. geiger2022 identifies Behler-Parrinello symmetry functions, ACE and SOAP as invariant representations of local atomic environments, and DimeNet as pre-computing triplet angles into scalars.
required_claims.caveat: geiger2022 presents this family as the baseline it argues AGAINST, not as its own mechanism; direction of citation matters. Neither verified source establishes what geometric information is SUFFICIENT - the universality result for distances, angles and dihedrals (GemNet, NeurIPS 2021) is not in this set, so the claim is scoreable at the level of 'this family exists and works this way' only.

required_claims.text: The other rotational treatment carries geometric tensor features of order l >= 1 through the network, constraining every operation to be equivariant

locations.geiger2022: Sec. 4.2; Sec. 4.3; Sec. 4.6; Sec. 6.1 Eq. 6; Sec. 7 Eqs. 15-16; Sec. 8 Eq. 27

required_claims.evidence: geiger2022: all data in the network is typed by how it transforms under the Euclidean group, using irreps of O(3), where l=0 is scalars, l=1 vectors and l=2 the symmetric traceless rank-2 part; Sec. 4.6 defines equivariance and proves that the composition of equivariant functions is equivariant, so constraining each component guarantees whole-network equivariance; spherical harmonics are equivariant with respect to the irrep of matching order (Eq. 6); the tensor product is bilinear and equivariant with selection rules on l and parity (Eq. 16); Eq. 27 states rotation, translation and inversion equivariance together. jacobs2025: recent GNNs such as NequIP, MACE and TeaNet work with highly expressive equivariant tensor representations and operate on them so as to preserve the proper symmetries, and in equivariant networks the additional neighbour attributes are vectors and tensors, giving an atom an environmentally dependent non-spherical character.
required_claims.independence: geiger2022 and jacobs2025 are independent for the mechanism statement.

required_claims.text: Locality is imposed by a finite interaction cutoff together with decomposition of total energy into per-atom contributions over local environments

locations.jacobs2025: Sec. 4.1; Sec. 4.3 para. 2; Sec. 4.5 para. 1; Sec. 9.1 para. 1; Sec. 4.4 final para.

required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025: the local environment of every atom is represented by an atomic environment featurization; each atom is assigned an energy determined by its type and its local environment; explicit AEFs describe atomic energy through interaction with all neighbours within a cutoff distance; standard MLIPs learn local descriptors for environments encompassing a radius of roughly 5-10 Angstrom, becoming much slower for longer ranges.
required_claims.caveat: Locality and message passing are in tension within the same source. jacobs2025 Sec. 4.4 notes that multilayer GNNs effectively couple atoms 3-4 nm apart, much longer than the ~1 nm or less of direct physical interaction in PBPs and explicit AEF MLIPs, which can cause significant memory and parallelization issues - motivating Allegro, which forgoes message passing on the graph altogether, and MACE, whose high body-order local features make two hops sufficient.

required_claims.text: Total energy is constructed as a sum of per-atom contributions, and the training loss must contain a term depending on that sum

locations.jacobs2025: Sec. 3 para. 1; Sec. 4.3 para. 2; Fig. 1; Fig. 2

required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025: an MLIP maps an atomic configuration to a total energy for that set of atoms; each training energy is a total energy for a whole molecule or crystal unit cell because almost no ab initio method allows easy formal decomposition of total energy into per-atom values, so the fitting loss typically must contain a term depending on the sum of energies of all atoms in each configuration; Figs. 1 and 2 show the summation explicitly.
required_claims.caveat: TERMINOLOGY GAP. No verified source in this set uses the term 'size extensivity' or states it as a design principle - jacobs2025 describes the summed structure without naming the property. The claim is worded to what is actually supported. Resolve by either (a) rewording the question from 'size extensivity' to 'per-atom energy decomposition', or (b) adding Behler, Chem. Rev. 121:10037 (2021), ref. [2] of jacobs2025, as a naming source after reading it.
required_claims.distractor_note: Do NOT cite gilmer2017 for this claim. Summed readouts appear in models it surveys (DTNN, Interaction Networks, GG-NN Eq. 4), but its own best variant uses set2set, chosen in Sec. 5.3 on the reasoning that it is more expressive than simply summing the final node states, and all 13 QM9 targets are normalized to mean 0 and variance 1 in Sec. 7. Its headline result is structurally non-additive.
required_claims.flag: coverage capped at partial until the terminology gap is resolved

required_claims.text: Symmetry can also be acquired non-architecturally, by training a generic non-equivariant model toward equivariance through a latent-space objective
required_claims.evidence: elhag2025: state-of-the-art models enforce roto-translational symmetries through equivariant architectures, described as a hard-wired inductive bias that can reduce flexibility, computational efficiency and scalability; TransIP instead guides a generic non-equivariant Transformer to learn SO(3)-equivariance by optimizing its representations in the embedding space, attaining performance comparable to equivariant baselines on OMol25 and a 40-60% improvement over a data-augmentation baseline across dataset sizes.
required_claims.caveat: Single-source claim, verified at abstract and conclusion level only. Related mechanisms in the same family (frame averaging, local-frame architectures) are NOT verified and must not be scored.

required_claims.text: Generalization to system sizes beyond the training distribution remains an open problem with the symmetry constraints already in place
required_claims.evidence: gilmer2017 names designing MPNNs that generalize to larger graphs than those in training as an important future direction, and gives two specific reasons why spatial information makes this harder: the pairwise distance distribution depends heavily on the number of atoms, and the most successful use of spatial information creates a fully connected graph in which the number of incoming messages also depends on the number of nodes; it proposes attention over incoming message vectors as a possible remedy. jacobs2025: the true domain of applicability of U-MLIPs is quite uncertain, with areas of major weakness that cannot easily be predicted in advance - a U-MLIP might give excellent diffusivities for 95% of materials and be quite far off for 5%.
required_claims.caveat: gilmer2017 is a 2017 molecular-property paper, not an MLIP paper, and its models are permutation-invariant and distance-based yet still fail this transfer - which is precisely why it is load-bearing. It does not test per-atom-energy MLIP architectures.
required_claims.distractor_note: An answer asserting that symmetry constraints deliver size transfer is wrong. jacobs2025 Sec. 7.5.3 lists an architecture that cannot capture the essential symmetries and physics as only ONE of two compounding causes of poor transferability; the other is training data that is not evenly distributed in structural or chemical space.

required_claims.text: The locality constraint fails where the physics is non-local, requiring explicit long-range electrostatic or dispersion terms, and its validity is condition-dependent
required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025 describes two strategies. First, implicit renormalization of long-range effects into short-range interactions, which works for homogeneous condensed-phase systems with strong screening; it reports Ceder et al.'s analysis that this success rests on local charge neutrality, which correlates with lower-energy states, while higher-energy states with weaker local charge neutrality have electrostatic interactions that are not well represented by short-range terms - so researchers should be very careful about using only short-range interactions for simulations exploring higher-energy states. Second, explicit long-range terms: Coulomb's law via maximally localized Wannier centres (DeepPot, SCFNN), and DFT-D3 vdW plus electrostatic corrections as explicit energy terms (AIMNet2, MACE-MP0, SO3LR). Fig. 8 decomposes total potential energy into local, dispersion, electrostatic and induction contributions.
required_claims.caveat: This is the boundary condition on Q18.C4 and Q18.C5: the locality ansatz is condition-dependent, not universal. An answer stating locality and per-atom decomposition as mechanisms without stating their failure regime is incomplete.

required_claims.text: Relaxing strict locality through explicit long-range corrections improves transferability to out-of-distribution chemical space, not merely in-distribution accuracy
required_claims.evidence: sanocki2025: the vastness of chemical space makes generalization a central challenge for MLIPs, whose usefulness is often limited by poor transferability to out-of-distribution samples; a systematic evaluation of MLIP architectures with long-range corrections across diverse chemical spaces finds such schemes essential not only for improving in-distribution performance but, more importantly, for enabling significant gains in transferability to unseen regions of chemical space.
required_claims.caveat: Verified at abstract level only; do not score internal quantitative detail. This is the ONLY claim in the set giving directional evidence that a constraint choice measurably improves out-of-distribution transfer, which is the second half of the question. Its direction is notable: the gain comes from RELAXING locality, not from adding a symmetry constraint.
